newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-TENDULKAR STROKES CONFIDENT 62 IN TOUR OPENER.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TENDULKAR STROKES CONFIDENT 62 IN TOUR OPENER.

text.p: Sachin Tendulkar stroked a confident 62 as his Indian cricketers enjoyed a satisfactory workout on Sunday's rain-affected second day of their three-day tour opener against Eastern Province.

Although rain halted play at St Georges Park shortly after tea for the second day in a row, India's top six batsmen all enjoyed useful time at the crease before captain Tendulkar declared their first innings closed at lunch on 335 for six.
With the first test against South Africa starting in Durban on Thursday, left-handed number three Saurav Ganguly was top scorer with 97 and Rahul Dravid weighed in with a breezy 31 not out.
Eastern Province then reached 108 for two in reply, with Louis Koen producing a well-struck 44 and opener Philip Amm an unbeaten 41.
Indian seamer Venkatesh Prasad generated impressive movement off the slow pitch to return one for 22 in 11 overs.
Ganguly, tantalisingly close to his 11th first-class century, was removed by the occasional seam bowling of former South African captain Kepler Wessels.
Having faced 203 balls and struck 12 fours amd three sixes, the left-hander cut Wessels low to backward point where Ashwell Prince completed a tidy catch.
Tendulkar and Mohammad Azharuddin then threatened to bat Eastern Province right out of the game as they embarked on an assured fourth-wicket partnership of 42.
Azharuddin was in fluent touch and raced to 20 from just 21 deliveries but then edged the fast-medium seam of Wikus Botha to second slip.
Tendulkar, who reached his 50 from 96 balls with six fours, was out driving at the pace of Mornantau Hayward to be caught by Wessels at first slip.
